Zurich Canada (1996) 50 CA4th 658, 667, 57 CR2d 781, 786] (c) [3:454] Compare—claims of negligent supervision: Nor does § 533 bar coverage for claims against an employer for negligent hiring, retention or supervision of the sexual harasser (because no “wilful act” by employer). [See David Kleis, Inc. v. Sup.Ct. (California Ins. Co.) (1995) 37 CA4th 1035, 1050, 44 CR2d 181, 190] (d) [3:455] Compare—duty to defend: But it may not excuse the insurer's duty to defend where the complaint alleges conduct that does not necessarily constitute sexual harassment or other “wilful” misconduct. [See Horace Mann Ins. Co. v. Barbara B. (1993) 4 C4th 1076, 1082, 17 CR2d 210, 214—allegations of unwanted touching by teacher gave rise to duty to defend] [3:456 - 3:464] Reserved. 5. [3:465] Employment Discrimination Claims: Whether CGL policies provide coverage for employment discrimination is subject to a similar analysis as claims for wrongful termination and sexual harassment: a.
